items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: I had an office in the ‘60s at Al Gallico’s office.

ctx.x: I think it’s very interesting that other people heard that you had a sound but you weren’t aware of it. It’s almost like critics naming styles of music but the musicians don’t know. I mean not that they don’t know but musicians were playing bebop but they didn’t call it bebop until the critics did.

Yeah. It was sort of – I think you know taking into consideration, you mentioned something very, very early on about how rewarding it was to write arrangements. But there was also a – it was – I recognized that my career would probably only last maybe twenty, thirty years. And I had an office in the ‘60s at Al Gallico’s office. You may not know who Al Gallico was but he was a publisher and he published “Stand By Your Man” and he was basically Billy – oh I can’t remember his name now. But every day Hugo…
